I don't know if I should be thankful for the free service (using the government health insurance) or if I was just unlucky to encounter a dentist who was incredibly grumpy, heavy-handed, rude, and completely unenthusiastic. It was nothing like the other reviews; I'd even give it a negative rating. The stars I'm giving are probably just to thank them for allowing me to use my government health insurance.

I had braces done elsewhere, and because of the braces, I had a lot of tartar buildup. Other clinics charge 900-1200 baht, so I came here using my government insurance. The dentist complained, "You should have gotten your braces done at the same place you got them. You shouldn't regret spending this much money if you're going to do it this way."

Yes, that's true. I'm not clueless; I should have gotten everything done at one clinic. I should have gotten my braces done at the same place I got them. And I'm not unaware that braces make scaling difficult and might not be completely thorough. I'm the patient, I'm the one suffering, I'm the one who will suffer if the dentist doesn't do their best. Do you think patients don't realize what they're doing?

But people without money just don't have money. Or is the dentist saying that if you don't have money, you shouldn't have gotten braces in the first place? You should know better than anyone that braces can have escalating costs. It's not just about regretting a small expense. Because if the patient had money, they wouldn't use their universal healthcare card for something that involves pain.

And during the procedure, I was in pain and cried because of the pain. The doctor said, "You don't have to cry." Seriously, telling someone in pain not to cry... well, can't we cry?

I know that if a patient cries, it makes the doctor feel discouraged and hesitant to continue, but saying, "You don't have to cry," what were they thinking? Do they have a lot of medical experience, but their empathy has completely vanished?

Or is it because it's universal healthcare that they treat people like this? Do poor people have to endure the rudeness and bad attitude of medical personnel? Why open a clinic that accepts universal healthcare if you're going to provide service with such a rude attitude? We don't expect coddling, but if you can't speak nicely to someone in pain, it's better to stay silent. When I went, there weren't many patients; I was the only one, no queue.

You're a doctor, you should know that the patient is the one in pain. Why say something so rude? And it's even worse to say it during the procedure. The patient can only hold their breath, enduring the pain while listening to such harsh words, and can't even cry because it would upset the doctor and prevent them from continuing.

But thank you for speaking so rudely. Because it made the second half of the teeth scaling procedure painless. I was so angry and frustrated with the people who called themselves doctors that I forgot the pain. It was awful.
